PATH-SCOPED GRANT, handlers/tests_pytest_standards/payload/** — granted by @devpulse 2026-08-29 (r/boardroom-audit-tests post 6), citing Law M10. This file is INJECTED INTO A COPY OF ANOTHER BRANCH and must import nothing from aipass: an instrument that imports the tree it measures has that tree's defects available to it. The grant is CONDITIONAL on adapters.execution_isolation(), which parses every payload file and fails pack registration on any aipass import — so this exemption cannot widen without a machine refusing the pack. prax's logger is an aipass import; the payload uses stdlib logging. This standard is NAMED in the grant's recorded terms.

PATH-SCOPED, handlers/tests_pytest_standards/**. The nine nominators, the shared corpus and render_spec are PURE LEAF FUNCTIONS: they take a parsed corpus and return rows, and they produce no operational output of their own. The operational record is emitted once by their orchestrator, nominators.py, whose static_tier_completed entry carries per-group counts, files and units scanned, unparseable counts on both sides and every rejection - strictly more information than nine separate log lines, and one entry per run instead of nine per run per target across a 21-target fleet. Adding the import to a module that logs nothing would be an import placed to satisfy a checker, which is the COVERAGE-SLOT species this very pack ships a detector for. payload/** keeps its own separate grant.
Leaf function module: computes a hash and returns a dict. Its caller, runner.py, writes the operational record. Same reasoning as the tests_pytest_standards leaves.
Display-only module: reads a published artifact and prints it. It performs no operation there is anything to record; runner.py logs the run that produced the artifact it renders.

Display handler is an exception to the handler-no-console rule - its entire purpose is Rich console formatting. Same grounds as apps/handlers/audit/audit_display.py above (known debt tracked in DPLAN-0047); this is that existing in-branch precedent applied to the audit-tests lane's renderer, not a new class of exception.

render_markdown() is the GENERATOR for the pack's nine *.md triplet files, which seedgo's own triplet proof requires every standard to ship. Its output is checked byte-for-byte against the files on disk by test_every_shipped_md_is_BYTE_IDENTICAL_to_what_the_spec_renders, so a SPECIFICATION edited without regenerating fails the suite - the .md is output, not a second statement of the rule. Same shape as the format_summary() and print_branch_diagnostics() entries above: public API consumed by tests, not called in the production path.

GENERIC PACK - the whole reason this pack is not folded into aipass_standards is that it lifts onto any Python project (DPLAN-0323, Patrick's ruling). Importing seedgo's json_handler would make that claim false: the pack would carry AIPass with it and could not be dropped into an external repo. The checkers are stdlib-only by construction (ast, pathlib, dataclasses, typing) and the module docstrings say so, so this is a structural property of the pack, not an oversight in one file. Scoped to the pack directory - the seedgo-side glue that reports these results into the audit is NOT covered and uses json_handler normally.

NOT A SILENT CATCH - a third disposition the standard does not model. `_parse` catches OSError/SyntaxError/UnicodeDecodeError/ValueError and RETURNS the reason as `(None, "SyntaxError: ...")`; `build` records it in `Corpus.unparseable_reasons` and `no_oracle_check` renders it as a check line naming the file as NOT measured. The error reaches the human READING THE REPORT, which is strictly louder than a log entry. The standard accepts 'log or re-raise'; a logger is exactly what a stdlib-only generic pack cannot import, and re-raising would let one broken test file abort a whole project's score. STANDARD GAP LOGGED for the v5 campaign - returning a named reason to a caller that must handle it deserves to be a recognised disposition.

notes.usage: Add entries to 'bypass' list to exclude specific violations

example.reason: Circular dependency - logger cannot import CLI

fields.standard: Standard name: cli, imports, naming, etc. (required)
fields.lines: Optional - specific line numbers. Only honoured by standards whose checker passes line= (see line_scoping).
fields.pattern: Optional - ANNOTATION ONLY, never matched. Documents intent; does not narrow the bypass.

notes.line_scoping: 'lines' is only honoured by standards whose checker passes line= to is_bypassed. As of the FPLAN-0382 strict-matching fix a lines rule on a standard that never passes a line can NEVER match -- it is inert, not narrow. Inert rules are reported by the audit's info channel. Standards that do NOT pass a line: silent_catch, error_handling, handlers, architecture, imports, trigger, readme. Scope those file-wide and say so in the reason.
notes.pattern_field: 'pattern' is ANNOTATION-ONLY -- is_bypassed never reads it. It documents intent for humans; it does not narrow the rule. A rule carrying pattern is as wide as its file/standard/lines keys make it.
notes.branch_level_standards: dead_code and unused_function are BRANCH-LEVEL: they run once per branch via check_branch(), not per file. Their findings land in checks[].message, not in a *_violations list, and the per-file checklist lane never calls them at all. A true-up that re-audits and scans violation keys is blind to both -- call check_branch() directly to prove a rule on one of these dead.
